name: Bordeaux
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Bordeaux: wine estate and négoce diligence, aerospace supply chains, provenance and dispute support.
hero_lede: Bordeaux is the commercial centre of the world's best-known fine wine region and a major French aerospace and defence base. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching Bordeaux, working from lawful sources and coordinating French counsel and authorised local professionals where work in France is required.
intro: Bordeaux is the prefecture of Gironde and the main city of Nouvelle-Aquitaine. The commune had about 268,000 residents in 2023, Bordeaux Métropole's 28 communes about 854,000, and the wider metropolitan area about 1.43 million, the sixth largest in France. The economy is dominated by services, but two sectors give the city international weight. It is the trading hub of a wine region of around 116,000 hectares, 57 appellations and some 10,000 producing estates. It is also an aerospace, space and defence centre where Dassault Aviation, ArianeGroup, Safran and Thales operate, with some 15,000 aeronautics jobs. The port on the Gironde estuary and Bordeaux-Mérignac airport connect the city to the Atlantic economy.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Bordeaux for reasons that track these sectors. Buyers of châteaux and vineyard land, lenders against wine stock, and importers appointing distributors need to understand ownership, family arrangements, reputation and financial position behind estates and trading houses. Collectors, auction houses and insurers raise provenance and authenticity questions about high-value bottles. Aerospace and defence primes and their foreign partners review suppliers in the Gironde subcontracting base for ownership, export control and integrity concerns. Disputes over distribution contracts, estate sales and partnerships, and asset recovery involving Bordeaux families and companies, call for careful research in French records and media.

matters.title: Château and vineyard acquisitions
matters.text: Buyers of Bordeaux estates need more than a valuation. We research the selling family or group, holding companies, related trading entities, litigation, liens visible in public records and reputation in the trade press, so investors and counsel understand who they are dealing with before signing.

matters.title: Négociant and distributor diligence
matters.text: Importers and retailers appointing Bordeaux trading houses or courtiers review their ownership, financial filings, disputes and market reputation. We also research counterparties in Asia, the United States and elsewhere that buy from Bordeaux, where allocation diversion and grey-market resale can breach distribution terms.

matters.title: Fine wine provenance questions
matters.text: Collectors, auction houses and insurers sometimes question the history of high-value Bordeaux bottles. We trace the chain of sellers and intermediaries through corporate records, auction catalogues, litigation and media, supporting experts and counsel who assess authenticity and the client's recourse.

matters.title: Aerospace supplier integrity reviews
matters.text: The Gironde aerospace and defence base relies on specialist subcontractors. We review ownership, foreign links, sanctions exposure, litigation and adverse media for suppliers and partners, helping primes and foreign buyers manage export control, security and anti-corruption obligations.

matters.title: Asset research in estate disputes
matters.text: Inheritance, partnership and creditor disputes involving Bordeaux families often turn on property and shares held through sociétés civiles and holding companies. We map those structures from public records and support counsel preparing proceedings or settlement negotiations in France or abroad.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Bordeaux
local_context.text: Commercial disputes between traders and companies in the area go to the Tribunal de commerce de Bordeaux, staffed by elected business judges, with appeals to the Cour d'appel de Bordeaux, which covers several departments of the south-west. The city also hosts a judicial court and the Cour administrative d'appel de Bordeaux for public law matters. Published decisions and insolvency notices are useful in counterparty and dispute research.

local_context.title: Commercial registry and chamber
local_context.text: Companies registered in the Bordeaux area are entered in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés kept by the greffe of the commercial court, with data also available nationally. The Chambre de commerce et d'industrie Bordeaux Gironde, founded in 1705 and headquartered at the Place de la Bourse, supports local business and is a point of reference for trade and export activity.

local_context.title: Wine trade structures
local_context.text: Bordeaux wine is commonly sold through a system in which estates release wine via brokers to négociant trading houses, which then distribute it worldwide. Ownership of estates frequently sits in family sociétés civiles, insurers, banks or luxury groups. Understanding which entity owns the land, the brand and the stock is often the first question in any transaction or dispute. Trading house accounts can also reveal stock exposure.

local_context.title: Aerospace and defence cluster
local_context.text: Aeronautics is Gironde's second-largest export sector after agri-food, according to the local planning agency. Defence and space programmes in the area, including military aircraft and launcher components, mean some suppliers handle classified or export-controlled work. Research on these companies is limited to open sources and is scoped with counsel to respect French national defence secrecy and export rules. Many suppliers are small, family-owned firms.

local_context.title: Local investigative work
local_context.text: Private investigation in France is regulated nationally, as described on our France page. Where a Bordeaux matter needs local enquiries, TDSC coordinates French investigators holding the required authorisation and works through the client's French counsel, which also governs how findings can be used in proceedings. Enquiries are limited to what is necessary and proportionate for the stated purpose, and personal data collected locally is documented so that it can be reviewed by counsel.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Bordeaux and works on Bordeaux matters from Nashville. We first agree with the client and French counsel what decision the work supports: an estate purchase, a distribution appointment, a provenance question, a supplier review or a dispute. Research draws on French company and insolvency records, published court decisions, land and property information obtained lawfully, wine trade press, auction records and media in French and English. Personal data is handled in line with the GDPR and French law, with a documented purpose for each enquiry. Any local enquiries are carried out by authorised French investigators, coordinated through counsel, and we do not approach classified defence information.

faqs.q: Can you identify who really owns a Bordeaux château?
faqs.a: Usually the estate sits in a société civile or company whose partners and managers appear in French public records, sometimes behind further holding companies in France or abroad. We trace those layers, combine them with trade press and media, and distinguish documented ownership from inference. Beneficial ownership register access in France is restricted, so counsel advises on what can be requested.

faqs.q: Which courts hear Bordeaux commercial disputes?
faqs.a: Disputes between businesses are generally heard by the Tribunal de commerce de Bordeaux, with appeals to the Cour d'appel de Bordeaux. Civil disputes not involving traders go to the judicial court, and public law disputes go to the administrative courts. Contracts may also select arbitration or courts elsewhere in France or abroad.

No. Authentication is a matter for specialist experts. TDSC researches the provenance chain: who sold the bottles, through which companies and auctions, and whether those parties have been involved in disputes or prosecutions. That research complements expert examination and helps counsel decide on recourse against sellers or intermediaries.

faqs.q: Can you review a supplier in the Bordeaux aerospace base?
faqs.a: Yes, using open sources. We review ownership, management, foreign links, sanctions and export control exposure, litigation and media. We do not seek classified or protected defence information, and we coordinate with the client's export compliance and legal teams on how findings are used. Findings are reported with sources so they can be documented.

faqs.q: Can TDSC carry out surveillance in Bordeaux?
faqs.a: TDSC does not hold a French investigator authorisation and does not conduct surveillance itself. Where a matter justifies local enquiries, we coordinate authorised French professionals through the client's counsel, within limits set by French privacy and employment law and the rules on admissible evidence. Any such work is documented.
